# asc_volume (Resource)

Manages a block volume through ASC.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "asc_volume" "example" {
  name          = "example-data"
  size          = "10Gi"
  storage_class = "standard"
  access_mode   = "ReadWriteOnce"

  tags = {
    env = "production"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `access_mode` (String) Access mode of the volume.
- `name` (String) Name of the volume, which identifies it in ASC.
- `size` (String) Requested capacity as a Kubernetes quantity, for example "10Gi". A larger value resizes the volume in place; ASC cannot shrink one.
- `storage_class` (String) Storage class backing the volume.

### Optional

- `tags` (Map of String) Tags applied to the volume. Tags are updated in place.

### Read-Only

- `annotations` (Map of String) Annotations ASC reports for the volume.
- `attached_to_vm` (String) Instance id of the virtual machine the volume is attached to, empty when it is detached. ASC reports the machine's uuid here, not its name.
- `labels` (Map of String) Labels ASC reports for the volume.
- `last_error` (String) Last error reported by iASC, empty when there is none.
- `size_bytes` (Number) Capacity in bytes. ASC may echo back a different but numerically equal spelling of size, so this is the value to compare against.
- `status` (String) Lifecycle status reported by ASC.
- `urn` (String) URN of the volume, which carries its uuid.
- `volume_mode` (String) Volume mode reported by ASC.
